content: 1. Norethindrone/Ethinyl Estradiol Monophasic Kit: Administer one active tablet orally daily for days 1 to 21, followed by one inert tablet daily (or no tablets) for days 22 to 28. Restart with a new pill pack after day 28. Refer to the package insert for specific dosing instructions for multiphasic, biphasic, and triphasic regimens. Follow the manufacturer’s color-coding for sequence. This medication is contraindicated in premenarcheal individuals. 2. Drug Interactions: Ethinyl Estradiol and Fezolinetant: Ethinyl estradiol increases fezolinetant levels by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Mifepristone and Norethindrone: Mifepristone increases norethindrone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Ethinyl Estradiol and Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir/Dasabuvir: Co-administration can lead to significant ALT elevations (>5x ULN, sometimes >20x ULN). Discontinue ethinyl estradiol-containing medications before starting hepatitis C combination therapy and restart approximately two weeks after completing the regimen. Acitretin and Norethindrone: Acitretin reduces norethindrone efficacy through an unknown mechanism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. This combination is contraindicated. Amobarbital and Ethinyl Estradiol: Amobarbital reduces ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternative or additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods. Ethinyl Estradiol and Anastrozole: Ethinyl estradiol reduces anastrozole efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid concurrent use. Apalutamide and Ethinyl Estradiol/Norethindrone: Apalutamide reduces the levels of these hormones by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternative or additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods. Armodafinil and Ethinyl Estradiol: Armodafinil reduces ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraceptive methods. Belzutifan and Norethindrone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Belzutifan reduces hormone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially causing contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding. Use effective nonhormonal contraception. Atazanavir and Ethinyl Estradiol: Atazanavir may alter estrogen plasma levels. Use alternative contraception. Bosentan and Norethindrone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Bosentan reduces hormone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraception. Brigatinib and Norethindrone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Brigatinib reduces hormone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least four months after the last dose. Butabarbital and Ethinyl Estradiol: Butabarbital reduces ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraception. Carbamazepine and Norethindrone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Carbamazepine reduces hormone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable; use nonhormonal methods. Calaspargase Pegol and Ethinyl Estradiol: This combination is not recommended due to potential indirect interactions. Use non-oral contraceptive methods. Ethinyl Estradiol and Exemestane: Ethinyl estradiol reduces exemestane efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid concurrent use. Fexinidazole and Norethindrone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Fexinidazole increases hormone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. Fosamprenavir and Ethinyl Estradiol: Co-administration may alter hormone levels and reduce virologic response. Use nonhormonal contraception. Fosphenytoin and Norethindrone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Fosphenytoin reduces hormone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable; use nonhormonal methods. Griseofulvin and Ethinyl Estradiol: Griseofulvin reduces ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraception. Ethinyl Estradiol and Heparin: Ethinyl estradiol reduces heparin efficacy, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated. Idelalisib and Norethindrone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Idelalisib increases hormone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. Indinavir and Ethinyl Estradiol: Indinavir may alter estrogen plasma levels. Use alternative contraception. Ivosidenib and Norethindrone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Ivosidenib reduces hormone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraception. Lenolisib and Ethinyl Estradiol: Use alternative contraception. Lesinurad and Norethindrone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Lesinurad reduces hormone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraception. Letrozole and Ethinyl Estradiol: Ethinyl estradiol reduces letrozole efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid concurrent use. Loratatinib and Norethindrone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Lorlatinib reduces hormone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraception. Lopinavir and Ethinyl Estradiol: Lopinavir may alter estrogen plasma levels. Use alternative contraception. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor and Norethindrone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor reduces hormone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable; use nonhormonal methods. Mavacamten and Norethindrone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Mavacamten reduces hormone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for four months after the last dose. Metyrapone and Ethinyl Estradiol: Ethinyl estradiol reduces metyrapone efficacy. Rifapentine and Norethindrone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Rifapentine reduces hormone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable; use nonhormonal methods. Repotrectinib and Ethinyl Estradiol: Repotrectinib reduces ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use nonhormonal contraception.
